Chicago Dealer Selling Lamborghini Urus for Less Money Than a New Mercedes SUV
14 photos
Photo: Instagram | motorcarsofchicago
Between us, it is not exactly the Urus SE Performante that we are looking at here, which is Lamborghini’s latest take on its popular model.
This one debuted earlier this year, and it remains the only Urus currently in production. It offers 801 hp (598 kW/812 ps) and 738 pound-feet (1,000 Nm) of torque in total from its upgraded 4.0-liter twin-turbocharged V8 plug-in hybrid powertrain. It an travel for 37 miles (60 km) in the EV mode, hits 62 mph (100 kph) in 3.4 seconds, and has a 194 mph (312 kph) top speed.
It is not even the Urus SE Performante’s predecessor, the Lamborghini Urus SE , which is one-tenth of a second slower than its successor and has an identical top speed. This version of the exotic crossover, which shares its roots with the demised Volkswagen Touareg, the aging Bentley Bentayga, and the old Audi Q7, among others, has 789 hp (589 kW/800 ps) and 701 pound-feet (950 Nm) of torque combined.
As you can likely tell from the images shared in the gallery, you are not even looking at the discontinued S or Performante versions of the Lamborghini Urus. These featured no electrification, came with 657 hp (490 kW/666 ps) and 627 pound-feet (850 Nm) of torque on tap. The Urus Performante hits 62 mph (100 kph) in 3.3 seconds, identical to the electrified Urus SE Performante, and the Urus S is 0.2 seconds slower. The top speed is 190 and 189 mph (306-305 kph), respectively.
Photo: Instagram | motorcarsofchicago By elimination, what we are left with is the original Lamborghini Urus . You know, as in the model that debuted back in 2017, hitting the assembly line that same year. It too featured a V8 with twin turbocharging and a 4.0-liter displacement, which was good for 641 hp (478 kW/650 ps). At 627 lb-ft (850 Nm) of torque, the thrust was identical to the S and Performante versions, and this model needed 3.6 seconds to reach 62 mph from a standstill, reaching a top speed of 190 mph (306 kph).
The pictured example is a 2020 model year car that features a Grigio Nimbus Metallic paint finish on the outside. But why is it orange? Because it has been wrapped. It also has a glossy black wrap on the hood and roof, as well as on other exterior components, rides on black V-spoke wheels, and sports red brake calipers. And for what it’s worth, it definitely looks very good on the outside, doesn’t it?
But what about the interior, you ask? Well, here, the pre-facelifted Lamborghini Urus in question has black leather upholstery with plenty of red stitching for contrast. It also features the Italian flag motif on the steering wheel, some metal trim on the dashboard, the Raging Bull’s corporate logo embroidered into the headrests, black pillars, a black headliner, a panoramic roof, multi-zone climate control, and three screens, including one for the HVAC system.
Photo: Instagram | motorcarsofchicago In one of the images, we can see the check engine light illuminated in the digital gauge cluster, though the vendor hasn’t said anything about it. In fact, other than the mileage, asking price, and the fact that it has been wrapped, it did not have anything else to say about this machine. The vehicle had in the region of 49,000 miles (~79,000 km) under its belt at the time of cataloging, so it has seen some action over the years.
A 2020 model year Lamborghini Urus usually sells from $140,000 to $220,000 in today’s used car market in the United States of America. Examples with 40,000-50,000+ (64,000-79,000+) miles are considered high-mileage cars, and they sit at the lower end of the market, whereas those that have fewer than 15,000 miles (24,000 km) tend to reach the $200K mark and break into it.
Therefore, the Urus pictured in the gallery should not be on the pricey side of things. But is that really the case? Well, we found it advertised by @motorcarsofchicago on Instagram with an asking price of $169,995 at the time of writing, and it is up to you to decide whether it is worth that sum.
As far as the Mercedes SUV reference in the title, this Urus costs less than a brand-new Mercedes-AMG G 63, which has an MSRP of $198,750, and it is also more affordable than the Mercedes-Maybach GLS 680, which starts at $185,000. Sure, these may not be its rivals, because the Urus takes on the Ferrari Purosangue and Aston Martin DBX, but price-wise, it is more affordable than some new crossovers/SUVs.
Now, if you have that kind of money lying around and the desire to park a Lamborghini Urus in your driveway, the you should reach out to the selling dealer with an offer. Who knows, maybe you might be able to score this 2020 Lamborghini Urus for less money than advertised. After all, what’s the worse that they can do? Say no?
